page.layout: One page of text in a single column; a large woodcut initial opens the first paragraph of the section; a narrow column of marginal argument headings ("Argumentum MEDIATOR. Propositio.") stands in the left margin beside the first lines. Running head at top, page number at top left.

main_text.p: propriamque Servandi rationem, qua JesusChristus noster Servator Salutem aeterna nobis acquisierit, esse ejus SATISFACTIONEM ET MERITUM, adeoq; statuo & confido Christum, ut sanctum Pontificem & sanctam victimam, sua passione & morte pro nostris peccatis justo Dei judicio satisfecisse, & poenas nobis ob peccata debitas in se ut SPONSOREM nostrum derivasse, adeoq; amissam Dei Gratiam & Vitae Aeternae praemium nobis esse promeritum. Quod ut sic statuam his S. literarum testimoniis, indeq; deductis argumentis convincor & impellor.
main_text.head: CAPITIS IV.
SECTIO I.
main_text.p: Argumentum MEDIATOR. Propositio.Vi ejusmodi Mediator & Pacificator est Dei & Hominum, ut dissidentes partes (Deum dico & Homines) utrinq; in novum amicitiae foedus vere restituit, & non minus Dei, quam nostri respectu aeternum foedus gratia sua morte sancivit, & redemtionis pretium pro nobis se dedit, ita ut nos de placata Dei ira certo persuasi audeamus

page.notes: Printed page with a large woodcut initial "Q" at the start of the section. Margin text on the left reads "Argumentum" (in italic, partly obscured), "MEDIATOR." and "Propositio." The last line is cut off at the foot of the page and continues on the next page; it is transcribed as printed. Some letters in the first lines are faint and the spacing around "SATISFACTIONEM ET MERITUM" is irregular, but the words are legible. Show-through from the reverse side is visible and was omitted.
